messages:
maya: heads up — scorecard deltas look flipped for a couple quantized runner jobs in CI. baseline says model B regressed but the diffpanel shows a positive +3% improvement. this feels wrong.

oliver: can you drop the run id / job link? and a tiny snippet of the payload if possible.

maya: run id ci-eval/2024-03-15-qt-73, job 5871. artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/5871. important bit from server payload: ```{ \"metric\": \"coverage\", \"old\": 0.742, \"new\": 0.715, \"delta\": 0.027 }``` frontend shows +0.027 not -0.027.

ci-bot: job 5871 finished (agent runner-5). image: ghcr.io/redwood/runner:staging-20240315, seed=42, sampler=weighted. artifacts: https://s3/.../5871.tar.gz.

tj: FYI we merged the sample-weighted-agg change last week (PR#2812) — it switched aggregator normalization to use sum(weights) instead of count. could be a sign/normalization mismatch.

maya: i didn't touch aggregator in the quant PR, but the runner's seed handling was tweaked in infra PR#2860. maybe the combination exposed an edge.

eva: reproduced locally by re-running the harness with use_sample_weights=true. when group size is 1 the aggregator sum(weights) becomes 0 in our old path (edge case), delta math ends up dividing by 0 -> fallback produced a positive artifact. minimal repro: ```python
weights = [0.0]
values = [0.715]
avg = sum(w*v for w,v in zip(weights, values)) / sum(weights)  # -> ZeroDivisionError or NaN fallback
```

ryan: assigning this to eng-ml. probable fix: coerce weights to float, enforce min_total_weight=1e-9 and treat empty/zero-weight groups as uniform fallback weight=1.0. also add explicit 'sample_count' and 'total_weight' fields to the aggregator output so frontend can sanity-check sign.

oliver: also check exporter layering: legacy export path (used by some CI backfills) still emits delta = old - new while the new API uses delta = new - old. frontend assumes new - old. if a run used legacy exporter, sign flips.

tj: good catch. that's probably why only some jobs look flipped. two failure modes: zero-sum weights and mixed delta sign convention between exporter versions.

maya: two follow-ups then: (1) patch aggregator to avoid zero weight artifact, (2) canonicalize delta sign at the API boundary and include metadata, (3) add an e2e test in runner CI to cover weight variants.

ci-bot: PR 2890 created by ryan: "scorecard: resilient weighted-aggregator + canonical delta". CI: running.

ev a: quick smoke on staging after merging ryan's patch — ran the quantized job series (same model, seed 42) and numbers now match backend payload sign and UI. staging artifacts: https://staging-evals/.../test-2890.

ryan: pushed small unit tests to cover weights=[0,0.5,1] and exporter compatibility. added payload fields: sample_count, total_weight, aggregator_version.

maya: :thumbsup: can we also add a UI note for runs produced before 2024-03-10 (when the exporter switch rolled out)? might confuse product folks if numbers retroactively appear inconsistent.

oliver: i'd avoid reprocessing historical runs for now. add a tooltip that shows "delta_signality: legacy-exporter" and a link to infra notes. design flagged.

tj: will monitor nightly evals for at least two days to confirm no regression.

maya: created INF-842 to track cleanup + e2e test: https://tracker/redwood/INF-842 — title: "scorecard: weighted aggregator sign artifacts for single-weight groups". assigning to ryan and oliver.

ryan: I'll follow up with a small canary rollout to prod tomorrow morning and add an alert if delta_sign flips unexpectedly.

eva: verified quantized T4-small runs on staging with PR2890 — diffs stable. keeping an eye on the 00:30 nightly that re-runs the full benchmark.

maya: thanks everyone. good catch on the exporter sign mismatch too — that would have been a nasty one to debug later. :bug: (reaction from oliver)

oliver: moving to close the thread — ping if nightlies show anything odd.
